deep_dive.title: RoSAMDepth: Robust Self-supervised Depth Estimation Leveraging Segment Anything Model
deep_dive.abstract: Robust depth estimation aims to maintain high-quality depths across diverse conditions. However, most existing methods estimate depth without taking into account the object-level information. As a result, the predicted depth may easily deviate within objects and become blurred under adverse conditions. To overcome this weakness, we propose RoSAMDepth, a novel framework that can assist robust self-supervised depth estimation in leveraging rich and diverse object-level priors from the Segment Anything Model (SAM). We focus on incorporating object-level information across three key aspects: a segment-guided representation contrasting method that injects object-level awareness into the feature representation space; an adaptive regional outlier masking strategy combined with a regional Gaussian likelihood loss that enforces regional depth smoothness; and an object-level reliability estimation strategy that mitigates the influence of unreliable supervision. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and diverse weather conditions demonstrate that our method produces sharper, more accurate depth predictions, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/xagao/RoSAMDepth.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 现有深度估计方法忽视物体级信息，导致物体内部深度易偏离、在恶劣条件下模糊。本文提出RoSAMDepth，借助分割一切模型（SAM）的丰富物体级先验辅助鲁棒自监督深度估计，通过分割引导的表示对比、自适应区域异常值处理等手段注入物体感知。实验表明该方法在多种条件下保持高质量深度、提升鲁棒性。其贡献在于将物体级先验有效融入自监督深度估计框架。

quick_skim.title: Efficacy of Monocular Depth Estimation in Lunar Environments
quick_skim.abstract: Recent advances in monocular depth estimation have demonstrated highly accurate 3D reconstructions within in-distribution terrestrial domains. This study investigates the efficacy of several state-of-the-art approaches to reconstruct out-of-distribution lunar environments using the NASA Ames Polar Optical Lunar Analog Reconstruction (POLAR) stereo dataset and Apollo 17 surface imagery. By leveraging these datasets, we establish a robust analog-to-field validation pipeline that evaluates quantitative performance against ground-truth physical analogs and qualitative performance against historical field data. Our results indicate that select state-of-the-art techniques can successfully generalize to produce high-fidelity relative 3D reconstructions of the unstructured lunar surface.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 单目深度估计在陆域同分布数据上已能高精度重建三维，但其在分布外环境中的泛化能力仍不清楚。本文利用NASA Ames POLAR月面模拟立体数据集与阿波罗17号影像，构建从模拟到实地的验证流程，对多种先进单目深度估计方法进行定量与定性评估。结果表明部分方法可成功泛化，生成高质量的相对三维重建。该工作为深度模型在极端未知环境中的零样本泛化提供了实证参考。

quick_skim.title: CASE: Concept-Aware Segmentation from Positive and Negative Visual Exemplars
quick_skim.abstract: Few-shot semantic segmentation typically identifies target objects based on positive support examples of a single semantic class. In practice, however, positive cues alone are often underspecified: for instance, "red cars" may be confused with cars of all colors, "vehicles" may include cars that should be excluded, and "material-defined objects" may span multiple categories. Fulfilling precise requests requires positive exemplars to provide inclusion evidence and negative exemplars to act as intent-defining constraints for exclusion and disambiguation. We formulate this setting as Specified Visual Prompt Segmentation (SVPS), where the target concept is specified by both positive and negative visual prompts. In this work, visual exemplars refer to support-image regions specified by bounding-box prompts. To study SVPS, we introduce CASE (Concept-Aware Segmentation from Positive and Negative Visual Exemplars), a benchmark built on COCO and PACO. CASE encompasses six category- and attribute-level task families: exclusion, isolation, union, attribute exclusion, attribute isolation, and attribute union. We evaluate SAM 3 under this setting and find that, despite its powerful positive-only few-shot segmentation capability, frozen SAM 3 does not consistently treat negative visual prompts as exclusion evidence. To address this, we present Concept Prompt Adaptation (CPA), a conservative LoRA-based adaptation baseline that improves positive-negative prompt interpretation on CASE while remaining competitive under positive-only few-shot segmentation. Code is available at https://github.com/WongKinYiu/FSS-CASE.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Few-shot segmentation with only positive exemplars is underspecified for concepts like red cars or material-defined objects. CASE formulates specified visual prompt segmentation, using negative exemplars as exclusion constraints alongside positive ones for concept-aware segmentation.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 少样本语义分割通常只依赖单一类别的正样本示例，难以精确表达颜色、材质等细粒度概念，容易产生误判。作者提出指定视觉提示分割的新设定，让正样本提供包含证据、负样本提供排除与消歧约束，并设计CASE框架融合正负视觉示例完成概念感知分割。实验表明该方法在细粒度概念分割上优于仅使用正样本的基线。该工作为开放词汇与少样本分割中的概念歧义消解提供了有效方案。

quick_skim.title: Spectral Invariant Fusion and Refinement for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation
quick_skim.abstract: Domain generalized semantic segmentation is challenging because it requires accurate dense prediction on unseen domains without any access to target-domain data during training. Existing methods improve transferability through data diversification, invariant learning, or direct use of foundation models, but they often struggle to simultaneously suppress domain-sensitive interference and preserve fine-grained spatial cues. In this work, we propose SIFR, a frequency-aware dual-stream framework that tackles domain shift at both the fusion and decoding stages. SIFR uses spectral modeling as a unified principle to regulate both heterogeneous prior interaction and dense decoder refinement. Instead of directly fusing frozen CLIP and DINOv2 features, SIFR performs spectral-guided invariant fusion to filter out domain-sensitive responses while preserving complementary semantic and structural information. In addition, SIFR incorporates a spectral decoder refinement module that stabilizes multi-scale decoder features through low-frequency statistics-based normalization and adaptive frequency selection, thereby reducing the propagation of residual domain bias in dense prediction. This design enables SIFR to jointly improve domain robustness and segmentation precision under severe distribution shifts. Extensive experiments on multiple DGSS benchmarks, including synthetic-to-real, real-to-real, and adverse-weather settings, demonstrate consistent improvements over previous state-of-the-art methods.
